skill.description: Guide Dify frontend refactoring for complex React components using hook extraction, component splitting, and incremental verification.

security_audit.summary: The static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, TypeScript examples, Object.keys, and ordinary callback names in documentation. I found no prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or malicious execution behavior in the cited files. The skill documents local Dify pnpm commands, so users should apply normal review before running project scripts.

content.value_statement: Large React components slow review, testing, and maintenance. This skill guides hook extraction, component splitting, and Dify-aligned verification.
actual_capabilities: Identifies when Dify React components exceed complexity or line-count thresholds.
Guides extraction of state, effects, data fetching, forms, and modal logic into hooks.
Shows component splitting patterns for headers, modals, lists, and workflow nodes.
Maps detected complexity features to incremental refactoring actions.
Defines verification steps using Dify lint, type check, test, and analyzer commands.
limitations: Designed for Dify frontend conventions, not general React architecture.
Requires access to the target codebase and existing Dify tooling.
Does not automatically rewrite files without agent or developer action.
May need adaptation for third-party wrappers or simple components.

use_cases.title: Prepare Complex Components For Tests
use_cases.description: Break down large Dify components before adding tests, so behavior is easier to isolate and verify.

use_cases.title: Standardize Dify Refactors
use_cases.description: Apply consistent hook, service, modal, form, and workflow node patterns across frontend changes.

use_cases.title: Review Refactoring Plans
use_cases.description: Check whether a proposed split preserves behavior, follows Dify conventions, and includes verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Assess a Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one complex component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Dify React component for complexity. Identify whether it should be refactored before testing and list the first safe extraction steps.

prompt_templates.title: Extract a Custom Hook
prompt_templates.scenario: Move related state and effects out of a component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this component by moving related state, effects, and handlers into a custom hook. Preserve behavior and Dify naming conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Split a Large UI
prompt_templates.scenario: Separate a large component into focused files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a component split for this large Dify UI. Separate orchestration, header, content, modal, and list responsibilities.

prompt_templates.title: Reduce Complexity Incrementally
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the component analysis output to create an incremental refactoring plan. Include verification after each extraction and note behavior risks.

output_examples.input: A Dify configuration component has 420 lines and many state groups.
output: Recommended splitting header, content, debug, and modal areas.
Moved model configuration state into a dedicated hook.
Added verification steps for complexity, linting, typing, and tests.

output_examples.input: A workflow node component mixes panel UI, interaction state, and service calls.
output: Suggested separate panel and node files.
Moved interaction handlers into a focused hook.
Kept service hooks aligned with Dify conventions.

output_examples.input: A form component repeats validation, submission, and modal logic.
output_examples.output: The result describes a form hook, a modal manager, and a verification sequence for behavior preservation.

best_practices: Run complexity analysis before deciding which extraction pattern to use.
Extract one responsibility at a time and verify behavior after each step.
Follow existing Dify folder, hook, service, and workflow naming conventions.
anti_patterns: Do not split simple components only to reduce line count.
Do not create many tiny hooks that separate tightly related state.
Do not change public props or behavior during structural cleanup.

faq.question: Does this skill edit code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides refactoring guidance for an agent or developer to apply.

faq.question: Which codebase is it designed for?
faq.answer: It targets the Dify frontend and its React, TypeScript, and pnpm tooling conventions.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it when component complexity is above 50, line count is above 300, or testing is blocked by structure.

faq.question: Can it help with custom hooks?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes how to extract related state, effects, data fetching, forms, and modal logic.

faq.question: Does it replace testing?
faq.answer: No. It recommends linting, type checks, tests, and manual verification after each extraction.

faq.question: Is it useful outside Dify?
faq.answer: Some React patterns transfer, but commands, paths, and examples are Dify-specific.
